state_vector.principle: A coordinate qualifies only if (a) it is computable from bars/volume at or before the completed decision bar, (b) it exists as a column somewhere in the repo OR is a stated arithmetic function of columns that exist, and (c) its provenance is a committed artifact. Fixed-percentage and fixed-clock quantities appear only as measurement rulers, never as triggers.

The true net-beta comparator (sum_j w_i w_j cov_i,j) does not exist as a risk object anywhere.

group_K_broken_RTH_data.note: F2_F12 rebuilds everything from session bars only (session_end filter), so overnight drift is excluded by construction. Any carried ticket's state must be rebuilt from the carry-day bars; basket_f4_paths._tape_for / sim.CarrySubstrate already own that tape for F4 but no panel exposes a carried ticket's own-path state.

estimand.marginal_value_of_continuing: For a single ticket at decision bar t, with s = the observable state vector and pi_t = the executable price (the engine's own rule: open of the first bar with et > t, clamped by min(open, level) when a level exists), define V(s) = the supremum over stopping times tau > t of E[ P_tau / pi_t - 1 | s ] restricted to exits the engine can actually execute (a bar open, next-bar-open timing, minus friction). Then: hold = V(s); reduce by rho = rho*V(s) (scale-free, no new information); add = V(s) - f_entry_side; switch to peer j = V(s_j) - V(s_i) - 2*f_side. cash = 0.
estimand.why_the_collapse_is_the_point: ALL FOUR candidate actions are functions of the SAME one scalar V(s) plus the friction of the action that creates new exposure. F1-F14 searched scale (how much), timing of the same scalar (when), and partialness (how much of the same scalar) - none of which can create EV once V(s) < 0 on the traded population. That is the structural reason every arm landed negative or within a few bps of hold.
estimand.what_shape_means: Not 'what threshold on s makes V(s) > 0'. Shape = (i) is V monotone in each coordinate; (ii) is the ordering stable across the two development blocks; (iii) how much of the raw E[fwd ret] is a pure exposure-length effect (arithmetic) vs state (choice); (iv) is the spread of V(s) inside the executable price noise. The last one is decisive: measured |next-open / prior-close - 1| has mean 0.29-0.39% and median 0.093-0.19% per bar [PROBE], versus state-conditional drifts of 0.5-4.4 bp per remaining minute - so only actions that change exposure for MANY minutes can ever pay for one execution step.
estimand.friction_constant_being_used: basket_sim.py _execute: side = bps / 20_000, ENTER shares = budget / (px*(1+side)), REDUCE/EXIT proceeds = sh*px*(1-side). So the label bps is the ROUND-TRIP cost: 100 bps = 50 bps per side, 150 bps = 75 bps per side. Every F1-F14 conclusion inherits this constant.

ideas.title: The decision collapse: every F1-F14 architecture is a re-parameterisation of one scalar (V(s)) plus fresh friction, which is why none of them found EV
ideas.mechanism: Holding pays no new friction. Reducing to cash realises the same V(s) at scale rho and pays no new friction (one exit either way). Adding pays an entry side. Switching pays an exit plus an entry. So EV can only be created by (a) identifying states where V(s) > 0, or (b) reducing exposure when V(s) < 0 - and (b) is arithmetic, not edge.
ideas.plausibility: It predicts three measured facts exactly, including two that look puzzling otherwise. (i) F4's partial scale-out is 'a wash against the matched same-trigger full exit' - predicted, because partial = rho x full at the same trigger. (ii) F6's 'withholding alone leaves EV per deployed dollar unchanged' - predicted, because withholding scales exposure and nothing else. (iii) HARVEST's +89 bps/day is exposure removal - predicted, and the arithmetic confirms 101 of the 89... see numbers.

evidence.harvest_arithmetic_verified: [ARTIFACT + recomputation] HARVEST_DIAG/SUMMARY.json A_pm_N2_hold_bps100 mean -0.039378 on avg_deployed 1.154388 -> -3.4112% per unit of exposure-time; times the all30 arm's 0.857369 = -2.9242%. Realised all30 mean -0.030436. Realised is 12.0 bps WORSE than the pure-deleveraging benchmark, so the touch-triggered exit removed exposure that was, if anything, slightly above-average - the +89 bps/day is exposure removal, not a better exit price.
evidence.f4_scaleout: [ARTIFACT] DIAGNOSTICS_20260924/F4_C1_surface_summary.json summary: only 2 of 74 cells beat the matched same-trigger full exit in BOTH blocks (A_pm_N2_R2_L15_w5_50_rest, +0.00082 b1 / +0.00074 b2 at 100 bps); block1_beats_matched = 38 of the surface, block2 = 8; mean_range_100bps = [-3.826%, -2.926%] - the whole 74-cell surface is negative.

ideas.what_prior_code_actually_tested: F4 (factory/scripts/basket_f4_scaleout.py + basket_f4_rules.py Trigger/ScaleOutRule) tested WHICH TRIGGER fires and WHAT FRACTION is sold; F5 (basket_f5_scalein.py ScaleInOnGain) tested ADD on a +trig% close with a cap; F6 (basket_f6.py) tested whether the reserve dollar goes to cash / equal split / state67 / state33. None of them ever estimated V(s) itself: no artifact in the repo reports an executable forward P&L conditional on state. The F2_F12 panel - the only state panel - carries NO forward P&L target at all (TARGETS = touch30, touch50, touch100, rem_mfe, rem_mae, nhba; forward_value is literally an alias of rem_mfe).
bugs_or_mismatches: The F2_F12 outcome vocabulary cannot express the estimand. rem_mfe/rem_mae are excursion extremes, and touch*/nhba/adverse_first are barrier crossings. None is a price you could receive. This is the central vocabulary gap: a state with high rem_mfe and negative expected close return is scored as 'good'.

F6's per_deployed_dollar rows exist for the redeployment arms but are missing for the p=1.00 full and p=0.50 cash rows, so the headline comparison ('withholding alone leaves EV per dollar unchanged') cannot be read off the artifact's own rows - it needs the reader to recompute r/avg_deployed. Cosmetic, but it is the load-bearing comparison.
ideas.smallest_study: Add one target column to the F2/F12 panel - `fwd_close_ret_t = close(session_end_bar)/close_t - 1` and `fwd_close_ret_to_next_open = close(session_end_bar)/open(next bar) - 1` - and one derived normaliser `live_bars_remaining`. Both are 3-line additions inside f2_f12.checkpoint_row, no new data, no simulation. Then table V(s) by state quintile x block. Output: one parquet + one JSON table. Runtime: minutes.
ideas.meaningful_result: Any (state, block) cell with mean fwd_close_ret net of a full round trip > 0 would falsify the current 'all cells negative' reading and locate the phenomenon's EV. Symmetrically, if the whole surface stays negative after the exposure-length term is divided out, the correct conclusion is that A_pm/T570 top-N buy-and-hold contains no EV at this friction - which is itself the decision-relevant answer, and it would end the family search rather than extend it.

ideas.title: The loss side, not the right tail: the population mean is set by a large adverse cohort, and the value ordering is monotone in retention-from-running-high
ideas.mechanism: The traded population is dominated by names that spike and then give the spike back. Value per unit of remaining exposure is monotone in how far below its own running high the ticket currently is: deep in the red = negative per-bar drift; near the high = non-negative. Because 60% of observations sit in the adverse cohort, that cohort - not the tail - determines the sign of the sleeve.
ideas.what_prior_code_actually_tested: RESEARCH_REPORT §4.4/§4.5 measured MFE/MAE capability versus leniency, and F4's own-path metrics (basket_f4_paths.path_metrics, F4_C1 path_metrics.json) are constructed per-plan (per trigger, per armour). The F2/F12 checkpoint panel (basket_f2_f12.py) measures retention as `dd_from_running_high`/`dd_from_day_high`, but the point of the panel is the target columns (touch30/50/100, rem_mfe, rem_mae, NHBA), not the marginal value of continuing. No artifact reports an executable forward P&L conditional on retention at a decision bar, so the monotone-in-retention value ordering has never been estimated - only probabilities of future barrier crossings.
ideas.missing: The engine's own-path MFE/MAE are recorded ONLY after the path completes (basket_sim._track_raw_path runs after the session loop, so tk.mfe/tk.mae/h_touch_et are stale or empty during the session). There is no causal intraday MFE/MAE/halt/pullback state in the decision interface. Any model must build its own running state inside the strategy (or from a panel).
